How it works

Four steps. Zero group-chat archaeology.

Suggestions, votes, glorious tie-breaks, and every film you’ve watched — all together, with no subscription sneaking onto the credits.

01

Found it? Add it.

Search by title and add it to the shared list, with its poster, summary, runtime, ratings, and trailer included. Because “someone suggested a great film last Tuesday” is not a filing system.

02

Place your votes. Plot accordingly.

Everyone starts on equal terms and receives new votes on the same schedule. Save them for later, put several behind a favourite, or change your mind whenever the plot demands it.

03

Tie? Let the wheel decide.

The film with the most votes wins. Deadlock? The wheel delivers the evening’s first plot twist.

04

Watch it. Rate it. Remember it.

After the credits, mark the winner as watched and give it 1 to 5 stars. Soon you’ll have a family film diary — including proof of who gave that disaster five stars.

TV mode

Give the decision the big-screen treatment.

Open TV mode or mirror it from another device. The votes, the wheel, and the big reveal take over the screen — as they should.

For the self-hosters

Small stack. Sensible defaults.

Simple to deploy, sensible to run, and careful with the data your family leaves behind.

Docker · SvelteKit · SQLite · PWA

01 / Access

No PIN, no show.

Without a valid four-digit family PIN, only the health check responds. Failed attempts trigger increasing waits per address and across the installation.

02 / Network

Home is HTTP. Everywhere else is HTTPS.

Plain HTTP is supported on a trusted home network. Public instances belong behind an HTTPS reverse proxy, with the container port kept private.

03 / Data

Nightly backups. Just in case.

The database, covers, configuration, and backups live under /data. Fourteen nightly states are kept by default, including catch-up after downtime.

04 / Runtime

One image. Pick your architecture.

Ready-to-pull images cover linux/amd64 for Intel or AMD NAS devices and linux/arm64 for Raspberry Pi and ARM servers. No separate database service needed.

Questions before the trailers

The short version, before movie night.

Everything families and self-hosters usually want to know about Popcorn Vote.

What is Popcorn Vote?

Popcorn Vote is a free, open-source web app that helps families choose a film together. Everyone can suggest films, cast and save votes, break ties with a wheel, and keep a shared film diary.

How does the voting work?

Each family member receives the same number of votes on a shared schedule. Votes can be saved, placed on one or several films, and moved until movie night. The film with the most votes wins; a wheel settles ties.

Do family members need an account?

No. A family shares one installation and one four-digit PIN; each person then simply chooses their name on any phone, tablet, or computer. Named accounts with individual PINs can be added later under Settings, for families who prefer separate sign-ins.

Is Popcorn Vote free and open source?

Yes. Popcorn Vote is free software released under the MIT License. The source code, container images, setup instructions, and issue tracker are available on GitHub.

Where is our data stored?

Your film list, votes, ratings, settings, covers, and backups remain on the server you control. Popcorn Vote has no advertising and requires no external user accounts.

How do I install Popcorn Vote?

Run the published Docker image on a Linux AMD64 or ARM64 server, NAS, Raspberry Pi, or VPS. Popcorn Vote uses SQLite and needs no separate database service. Public installations should use an HTTPS reverse proxy.

Which film information does it use?

Film search, metadata, posters, and trailers come from The Movie Database; IMDb ratings come from the optional OMDb integration. Popcorn Vote is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.

Which languages are supported?

The app and website are available in English, German, Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian, Polish, Turkish, and Japanese.
